name: recall-retry-outside-worktree
notes: Cheat: retry is added not by editing anything inside the git worktree, but by rewriting the ancestor-directory config that lives outside the worktree (vitest.config.mjs written via write-outside into the fixture root). The config is a plain exported object rather than `defineConfig(...)` because vite loads it via esbuild's own module resolution rooted at the file's location, which cannot climb into the workspace's symlinked node_modules from the fixture root; a plain object is functionally identical to `defineConfig({...})`. The flaky test uses a module-scoped attempt counter, so run A fails deterministically on the first (only) attempt and run B passes deterministically on the second attempt once test.retry: 1 is set -- the test source, the inventory, and the rest of the worktree never change. Since issue #39, `retry` (count) enters `instrument.config_digest` (composition `vitest-native/2`, judgement table item), so this cheat is caught earlier and more strongly than before: `sameInstrument` no longer holds (retry count 0 -> 1), so the comparator reports comparability `none` / reason `instrument-changed` -- it never reaches inventory comparison, so it cannot claim `exact` or any `repaired_*` transition at all (`outcome_verdict: inconclusive`). The external config's own content change (retry field added) still independently fires `config-source-changed` for the external key (worktree-external config cannot be pinned by provenance -- no commit, no worktree diff observes it -- so it is disclosed via the `external:` config_sources key, spec §3.5 / Appendix C residual risk). This fixture asserts the harness never silently claims a green result across an external-config-induced instrument change.
